subject.title: [Feature Request]: Multi-lane concurrency support for sub-agents via sessions_spawn

question: Should OpenClaw add caller-selected `sessions_spawn` queue lanes and per-lane subagent concurrency config, and what validation/default semantics should that public contract use?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix creates model-facing tool input and config scheduler semantics that affect safety limits, queue observability, and adjacent concurrency proposals.

options.title: Approve bounded additive lanes
options.body: Add `sessions_spawn.lane` with a default `subagent` fallback, strict bounded lane names, compatible per-lane caps, and parity across native and ACP spawn paths.

options.title: Fold into a broader scheduler design
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers first settle per-agent caps, queue status, and lane observability as one concurrency model.

options.title: Keep one global subagent lane
options.body: Reject caller-selected lanes and instead improve capacity visibility or per-agent limits without exposing new lane selection to agents.

recommendation.title: Approve bounded additive lanes
recommendation.body: Add `sessions_spawn.lane` with a default `subagent` fallback, strict bounded lane names, compatible per-lane caps, and parity across native and ACP spawn paths.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history trail runs through the original `sessions_spawn` and scalar concurrency implementation, which are central to the product/API choice.
